en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
Naggavagga 29.
The Training Rule on the Transgression of Time:
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the family supporting the bhikkhunī Thullanandā said to her:
"If we are able, noble lady, we shall give robe-cloth to the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs.
At that time, the bhikkhunīs who had completed the rains residence gathered together, desiring to divide the robe-cloth.
The bhikkhunī Thullanandā said this to those bhikkhunīs:
“Wait, noble ladies; there is an expectation of robe-cloth for the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs.
The bhikkhunīs said this to the bhikkhunī Thullanandā:
“Go, venerable lady, and find out about that robe-cloth.
The bhikkhunī Thullanandā went to that family; having arrived, she said this to those people:
“Give, friends, robe-cloth for the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs.”
“Noble lady, we are not able to give robe-cloth to the community of bhikkhunīs.
The bhikkhunī Thullanandā reported this matter to the bhikkhunīs.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [as before]... complained, grumbled, and became indignant, saying:
“How can the noble lady Thullanandā, on account of a weak expectation of robe-cloth, allow the robe season to pass by?
… [as before] … “Is it true, monks, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, on account of a weak expectation of robe-cloth, allows the robe season to pass by?
“It is true, Blessed One.”
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How indeed, monks, can the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, on account of a weak expectation for robe-cloth, allow the robe season to pass by?
This, monks, is neither for the inspiration of those without faith nor for the increase of the faith of those who have it…” [and so forth].
And furthermore, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:
“Whichever bhikkhunī, however, should let the robe season pass by because of a weak expectation of robe-cloth, that is an offense entailing confession (pācittiya). Whichever bhikkhunī...
[as above].
Whichever [nun] of such a kind... "a nun" ...pe...
this is the nun intended in this context.
"Expectation regarding a weak robe" means that the statement "If we are able, we will give; we will make it" has been broken.
"The time for robes" means...
When the Kathina has not been spread, it is the last month of the rainy season; when the Kathina has been spread, it is five months.
"Should he let the robe-season pass" means:
if he lets the last day of the rainy season pass while the Kathina has not been spread, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If, when the kaṭhina has been spread, she lets the day for the removal of the kaṭhina pass by, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If, regarding a weak robe-material, perceiving it as weak robe-material, she lets the robe-season pass by, there is an offense of expiation.
If, regarding a weak robe-material, being doubtful about it, she lets the robe-season pass by, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If it is a weak robe-material, but she perceives it as not weak, and she lets the robe-season pass by, there is no offense.
If it is not weak robe-material, but she perceives it as weak, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If it is not weak robe-material, but she is doubtful, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If it is a robe that is not of poor quality, and one perceives it as such,
there is no offense.
There is no offense if one prevents [the gift] by pointing out its advantages.
"In the case of one who is insane,
or in the case of one who is a first-offender.
The ninth training rule is concluded.
